sections.h2: Who sends the property tax bill for a Tyler house?
sections.html:
The Smith County Tax Office bills and collects property tax for every taxing unit in the county, including the City of Tyler. The office is at 1517 W. Front St., Tyler, TX 75702, with a mailing address of P.O. Box 2011, and the number is (903) 590-2920.

The City of Tyler lists office hours of 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., open through lunch. One Tyler bill can therefore carry several lines: the city, Smith County, Tyler Junior College and a school district. Which school district appears depends on the address, because the city notes that some Tyler properties sit in Whitehouse ISD or Chapel Hill ISD instead of Tyler ISD.

sections.h2: What are the Tyler property tax rates?
sections.html:
The City of Tyler's tax page prints the 2026-2027 rates as $0.242063 for the city, $0.374088 for Smith County, $0.210312 for Tyler Junior College and $0.835000 for Tyler ISD. Smith County's own rate table lists the same figures for tax year 2026 as adopted rates.

sections.h2: How has the Tyler city tax rate changed over time?
sections.html:
The city says it has cut its rate by more than 50 percent since the mid 1990s: its history table starts at $0.5336 for 1994-95 and reaches a low of $0.1990 in 2007-08. The rate then rose to $0.2699 in 2021-22 before dropping each year to $0.236452 in 2025-26.

The 2026-27 rate of $0.242063 is a step up from the prior year, and the same Smith County table shows the city's rate sitting above its no-new-revenue rate of 0.232965. The city also says it continues a two-cent commitment of its tax rate to the street fund, equal to $2.4 million.

  • 2007-08: $0.1990
  • 2021-22: $0.2699
  • 2025-26: $0.236452
  • 2026-27: $0.242063

sections.h2: What is Tyler like for a seller?
sections.html:
Tyler is a Smith County city with 113,723 residents as of July 1, 2025 on 57.45 square miles of land, according to the Census Bureau. Its population grew 7.4 percent from the April 2020 base.

  • Median value of owner-occupied homes, 2020-2024: $235,300.
  • Owner-occupied housing unit rate: 55.4 percent.
  • Median selected monthly owner costs with a mortgage: $1,743; without one: $664.
  • Median gross rent: $1,252.
  • Median household income: $67,486 (2024 dollars).

Health care and social assistance receipts of about $3.47 billion in 2022 are among the largest lines on the city's QuickFacts page, the largest of the service lines it lists.

sections.h2: When are Tyler property taxes due?
sections.html:
Texas bills go out around October 1 and payment is due on receipt, but the penalty-free window runs through January 31. Taxes still unpaid on February 1 are delinquent, according to the Comptroller.

Once delinquent, the collector adds a six percent penalty and one percent interest, penalty grows one percent a month until July 1 when it reaches 12 percent, and interest keeps running at one percent a month. A taxing unit's attorney can add up to 20 percent more. Homeowners may qualify to split the bill: the first half by November 30 and the second half by June 30 of the following year, under the calendar the Comptroller publishes, which the Smith County office can confirm for your bill.

sections.h2: What exemptions can a Tyler homeowner claim?
sections.html:
School districts must give a $140,000 residence homestead exemption under state law, and homeowners age 65 or older or disabled get an additional $60,000 from school districts. The application deadline for most exemptions is before May 1 with the appraisal district.

Other state-level protections apply to Tyler homes too:

  • A 10 percent annual cap on appraised value increases for a residence homestead, starting the year after the exemption is first qualified.
  • A school-tax ceiling for owners 65 or older or disabled, which can follow the owner to a new Texas homestead.
  • Disabled veteran exemptions of up to $5,000, $7,500, $10,000 or $12,000 depending on rating, and a total exemption for a 100 percent disabled veteran's homestead.

Cities, counties and colleges may adopt local exemptions, and the amounts for the City of Tyler, Smith County and Tyler Junior College are not printed on the pages above. Ask the Smith County Appraisal District for the current local percentages.

sections.h2: How do you protest a Tyler appraisal?
sections.html:
File with the appraisal review board by May 15 or within 30 days of the notice's delivery, whichever is later. Notices for single-family homesteads are mailed around April 1, and the board starts hearing protests around mid May.

If the board's decision does not satisfy you, the Comptroller lists district court, binding arbitration, or the State Office of Administrative Hearings for values over $1,000,000. An owner who appeals still has to pay at least the undisputed tax before the delinquency date, so a protest does not pause the bill.

sections.h2: How are Tyler property taxes handled when you sell?
sections.html:
The tax lien attaches on January 1 each year, and the owner on that date is liable for the year's tax. Your sale contract decides how the year's bill is split between buyer and seller at closing.

If you sell mid-year, ask the Smith County Tax Office for the amount due before closing and get the payoff figure in writing. A homestead exemption does not transfer on its own: a buyer who closes after January 1 may claim it for the rest of that year if the seller did not receive it, and heirs without a recorded deed must file an affidavit of ownership interest and the owner's death certificate.

faqs.q: What is the City of Tyler property tax rate?
faqs.a: The City of Tyler lists $0.242063 for 2026-2027, and Smith County's table shows the same figure as the adopted 2026 rate. Your full bill also includes county, junior college and school district rates.

faqs.q: Who do I pay property tax to in Tyler?
faqs.a: Pay the Smith County Tax Office at 1517 W. Front St., Tyler, or call (903) 590-2920. The county office collects for all taxing jurisdictions in Smith County, including the City of Tyler.

faqs.q: When do Tyler property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: February 1 for most bills. State rules call for payment by January 31, and unpaid tax on February 1 picks up a six percent penalty and one percent interest.

faqs.q: Is every Tyler address in Tyler ISD?
faqs.a: No. The city notes that some properties inside Tyler are in Whitehouse ISD or Chapel Hill ISD. Check your tax statement to see which school district rate applies.

faqs.q: How much is the homestead exemption in Tyler?
faqs.a: School districts must give $140,000 off a residence homestead's value, plus $60,000 more for owners 65 or older or disabled. Local exemption amounts for the city and county are a question for the Smith County Appraisal District.
